summary.overview: An Inspector Calls is a famous 1945 stage play by English dramatist J.B. Priestley. Set in 1912 in the fictional industrial city of Brumley, it examines the affluent Birling family, whose comfortable celebratory dinner party is abruptly interrupted by the arrival of a mysterious police inspector investigating the suicide of a young working-class woman named Eva Smith.
summary.plot_summary: The play opens with Arthur Birling celebrating his daughter Sheila's engagement to Gerald Croft, expressing capitalist views on individualism and business ('community and all that nonsense'). Suddenly, Inspector Goole arrives, announcing that a young woman named Eva Smith (later known as Daisy Renton) has died by suicide after drinking disinfectant. Through a meticulous chain of interrogation, the Inspector reveals how each family member—and Gerald—played a contributory role in her downward spiral: Arthur Birling fired her for demanding higher wages; Sheila had her dismissed from her next job out of jealousy; Gerald kept her as his mistress before discarding her; Eric forced himself upon her and stole money to support her; and Sybil Birling refused her charitable aid when she was pregnant and desperate. As the Inspector departs with a stern warning about social responsibility, Gerald returns with news that no Inspector Goole exists at the local police force and no girl has recently died. While the older Birlings (Arthur and Sybil) and Gerald dismiss the entire ordeal as a hoax and celebrate, the younger generation (Sheila and Eric) remain deeply shaken by their moral guilt. The play concludes with a chilling climax: a real phone call announces that a young woman has just died by suicide, and a real inspector is on his way to interrogate them.

cbt_questions.question: Who is the author of the play 'An Inspector Calls'?
options: A) George Bernard Shaw
B) J.B. Priestley
C) Oscar Wilde
D) Arthur Miller
cbt_questions.answer: B) J.B. Priestley

cbt_questions.question: In what year was the play written and first performed?
In what year is the play's action specifically set?
What is the name of the fictional industrial city where the play takes place?
options: A) Manchester
B) Brumley
C) Liverpool
D) Birmingham
cbt_questions.answer: B) Brumley

cbt_questions.question: What occasion is the Birling family celebrating at the beginning of the play?
options: A) Arthur Birling's knighthood
B) Sheila Birling and Gerald Croft's engagement
C) Eric Birling's birthday
D) A successful business merger
cbt_questions.answer: B) Sheila Birling and Gerald Croft's engagement

cbt_questions.question: What is the name of the company owned by Arthur Birling?
options: A) Birling & Co.
B) Croft & Birling Ltd.
C) Brumley Works
D) Imperial Steels
cbt_questions.answer: A) Birling & Co.

cbt_questions.question: Which family does Gerald Croft belong to, and why is the alliance important to Arthur Birling?
options: A) The Birlings; it keeps money in the family
B) Crofts Limited; it is a larger, rival company that could mean a potential business merger
C) The royal family; it brings political power
D) The local church; it brings moral respectability
cbt_questions.answer: B) Crofts Limited; it is a larger, rival company that could mean a potential business merger

cbt_questions.question: What political and economic view does Arthur Birling aggressively champion early in the play?
options: A) Socialism
B) Radical communism
C) Capitalistic individualism ('every man for himself')
D) Absolute monarchy
cbt_questions.answer: C) Capitalistic individualism ('every man for himself')

cbt_questions.question: Which historical events does Arthur Birling foolishly mock and dismiss as impossible in his opening dinner speech?
options: A) The sinking of the Titanic and a future world war
B) The invention of the airplane and telephone
C) The collapse of the British monarchy
D) The Russian Revolution
cbt_questions.answer: A) The sinking of the Titanic and a future world war

cbt_questions.question: What is the name of the inspector who arrives at the Birling household?
options: A) Inspector Poole
B) Inspector Goole
C) Inspector Cole
D) Inspector Sharp
cbt_questions.answer: B) Inspector Goole

cbt_questions.question: What tragic news does the Inspector bring when he first enters?
options: A) A local bank has crashed
B) A young woman named Eva Smith has committed suicide by drinking disinfectant
C) A factory fire has destroyed Birling & Co.
D) World War I has officially broken out
cbt_questions.answer: B) A young woman named Eva Smith has committed suicide by drinking disinfectant

cbt_questions.question: Why did Arthur Birling fire Eva Smith from his factory in 1910?
options: A) She stole company money
B) She led a strike demanding higher wages (twenty-five shillings a week)
C) She insulted his wife
D) She was habitually late for work
cbt_questions.answer: B) She led a strike demanding higher wages (twenty-five shillings a week)

cbt_questions.question: How does Arthur Birling justify firing Eva Smith?
options: A) He claims he had to make an example to keep labor costs down and run a profitable business
B) He admits he acted out of personal malice
C) He says she was completely unqualified
D) He claims she attacked a manager
cbt_questions.answer: A) He claims he had to make an example to keep labor costs down and run a profitable business

cbt_questions.question: What role did Sheila Birling play in Eva Smith's downfall?
options: A) She fired her from Milwards clothing store out of petty jealousy and bad temper
B) She stole money and framed Eva
C) She bullied her at school
D) She refused to give her food
cbt_questions.answer: A) She fired her from Milwards clothing store out of petty jealousy and bad temper

cbt_questions.question: What alias did Eva Smith adopt when she met Gerald Croft?
options: A) Rose Maybud
B) Daisy Renton
C) Clara Smith
D) Martha Jones
cbt_questions.answer: B) Daisy Renton

cbt_questions.question: Where did Gerald Croft meet Daisy Renton, and what did he do for her?
options: A) At a church; he helped her find a job
B) At the Palace Music Hall bar; he rescued her from Alderman Meggarty's unwanted advances, housed her, and made her his mistress
C) On a ship to America; he paid for her ticket
D) In a park; he gave her charity money
cbt_questions.answer: B) At the Palace Music Hall bar; he rescued her from Alderman Meggarty's unwanted advances, housed her, and made her his mistress

cbt_questions.question: How does Gerald feel when he breaks off his relationship with Daisy Renton?
options: A) He feels completely indifferent and heartless
B) He genuinely cared for her and kept her as a cherished friend
C) He genuinely cared for her as a mistress when it suited him, but discarded her when he had to leave for the summer
D) He hated her from the start
cbt_questions.answer: C) He genuinely cared for her as a mistress when it suited him, but discarded her when he had to leave for the summer

cbt_questions.question: Who is the father of Eva Smith's unborn child?
options: A) Gerald Croft
B) Arthur Birling
C) Eric Birling
D) Inspector Goole
cbt_questions.answer: C) Eric Birling

cbt_questions.question: How did Eric Birling fund his financial support for Eva Smith when she was pregnant?
options: A) He earned extra money working overtime
B) He stole fifty pounds from his father's office safe
C) He won money gambling
D) He borrowed it from Gerald
cbt_questions.answer: B) He stole fifty pounds from his father's office safe

cbt_questions.question: Why did Eva Smith refuse to accept money from Eric when she discovered it was stolen?
options: A) She was wealthy on her own
B) She had high moral integrity and knew the money was stolen
C) She hated Eric
D) She wanted money from Gerald instead
cbt_questions.answer: B) She had high moral integrity and knew the money was stolen

cbt_questions.question: What is Sybil Birling's connection to Eva Smith?
options: A) Sybil was her former schoolteacher
B) As head of the Brumley Women's Charity Organization, Sybil cruelly turned down Eva's application for financial aid
C) Sybil hired her as a personal maid
D) Sybil is secretly her biological aunt
cbt_questions.answer: B) As head of the Brumley Women's Charity Organization, Sybil cruelly turned down Eva's application for financial aid

cbt_questions.question: Why does Sybil Birling reject Eva Smith's appeal for charity?
options: A) The committee had run out of funds completely
B) Eva used the name 'Mrs. Birling,' which Sybil viewed as impertinent and offensive
C) Eva refused to answer questions
D) Sybil knew Eric was the father
cbt_questions.answer: B) Eva Use the name 'Mrs. Birling,' which Sybil viewed as impertinent and offensive

cbt_questions.question: Whom does Sybil Birling blame entirely for the girl's death just before she realizes Eric is involved?
options: A) Herself
B) The father of the child, insisting he should be publicly made an example of and forced to confess
C) Arthur Birling
D) The Inspector
cbt_questions.answer: B) The father of the child, insisting he should be publicly made an example of and forced to confess

cbt_questions.question: How does Sheila's reaction to the Inspector's investigation differ from her parents' reaction?
options: A) She remains cold and unrepentant
B) She immediately accepts moral responsibility, feels deep remorse, and matures significantly
C) She faints and forgets everything
D) She joins her father in attacking the Inspector
cbt_questions.answer: B) She immediately accepts moral responsibility, feels deep remorse, and matures significantly

cbt_questions.question: What generational divide is heavily emphasized throughout the play?
options: A) Between the rich and the poor
B) Between the older generation (inflexible, unrepentant capitalists) and the younger generation (impressionable, socially conscious)
C) Between men and women
D) Between British citizens and foreigners
cbt_questions.answer: B) Between the older generation (inflexible, unrepentant capitalists) and the younger generation (impressionable, socially conscious)

cbt_questions.question: What is symbolic about the name 'Goole'?
options: A) It sounds like 'gold', representing greed
B) It sounds like 'ghoul', suggesting he is a spirit, ghost, or supernatural judge of conscience
C) It means 'good citizen'
D) It is a common Scottish surname
cbt_questions.answer: B) It sounds like 'ghoul', suggesting he is a spirit, ghost, or supernatural judge of conscience

cbt_questions.question: What famous socialist warning does Inspector Goole deliver in his final speech?
options: A) 'We are responsible for each other... if men will not learn that lesson, then they will be taught it in fire and blood and anguish.'
B) 'Capitalism will destroy the world if taxes are raised.'
C) 'Always look after your own family first.'
D) 'Government should control every factory in England.'
cbt_questions.answer: A) 'We are responsible for each other... if men will not learn that lesson, then they will be taught it in fire and blood and anguish.'

cbt_questions.question: What startling discovery does Gerald Croft make after the Inspector leaves?
options: A) That Eva Smith is still alive
B) That there is no Inspector Goole registered with the Brumley police force
C) That Arthur Birling is bankrupt
D) That Sheila is married
cbt_questions.answer: B) That there is no Inspector Goole registered with the Brumley police force

cbt_questions.question: What further revelation does a phone call or local check confirm regarding the girl?
options: A) A girl died in the infirmary, but multiple photographs showed different girls, implying it might have been several different women
B) No girl has committed suicide in Brumley for years
C) Eva Smith was actually a fictitious person
D) The police have arrested Eric
cbt_questions.answer: A) A girl died in the infirmary, but multiple photographs showed different girls, implying it might have been several different women

cbt_questions.question: How do Arthur and Sybil Birling react once they suspect the Inspector was a fake?
options: A) They repent and change their lifestyle
B) They are immensely relieved, laugh it off, and refuse to accept any moral guilt
C) They call the police to report Gerald
D) They leave the country
cbt_questions.answer: B) They are immensely relieved, laugh it off, and refuse to accept any moral guilt

cbt_questions.question: How do Sheila and Eric react to the news that the Inspector might have been a hoax?
options: A) They join their parents in celebrating
B) They remain deeply troubled, recognizing that whether the inspector was real or fake, their immoral actions still happened
C) They run away from home
D) They demand Gerald break off the engagement
cbt_questions.answer: B) They remain deeply troubled, recognizing that whether the inspector was real or fake, their immoral actions still happened

cbt_questions.question: What shocking final twist occurs at the very end of the play?
options: A) The house catches fire
B) Arthur Birling receives a phone call stating a real girl has just died by suicide, and a real police inspector is on his way to question them
C) Inspector Goole returns with handcuffs
D) Sheila announces she is leaving
cbt_questions.answer: B) Arthur Birling receives a phone call stating a real girl has just died by suicide, and a real police inspector is on his way to question them

cbt_questions.question: What dramatic genre best describes 'An Inspector Calls'?
options: A) Slapstick comedy
B) A well-made play / Morality play / Detective mystery thriller
C) Science fiction epic
D) Historical romance
cbt_questions.answer: B) A well-made play / Morality play / Detective mystery thriller

cbt_questions.question: What theatrical device does Priestley use to maintain tension and unity of place?
options: A) Multiple revolving stage sets
B) A single dining room set that remains lit throughout while the surrounding stage is in darkness
C) Actors entering from the audience seats
D) Silent film projections
cbt_questions.answer: B) A single dining room set that remains lit throughout while the surrounding stage is in darkness

cbt_questions.question: What does the lighting change from 'pink and intimate' to 'brighter and harder' signify when the Inspector enters?
options: A) The sun is coming up
B) The shift from comfortable bourgeois illusion and rose-colored self-deception to harsh truth and exposure
C) A power outage in Brumley
D) The transition to a party atmosphere
cbt_questions.answer: B) The shift from comfortable bourgeois illusion and rose-colored self-deception to harsh truth and exposure

cbt_questions.question: What does Arthur Birling's obsession with respectability and his impending knighthood highlight?
options: A) His deep Christian charity
B) His shallow social ambition and bourgeois materialism
C) His military heroism
D) His dedication to working-class welfare
cbt_questions.answer: B) His shallow social ambition and bourgeois materialism

cbt_questions.question: Which character acts as the Inspector's primary foil, aggressively challenging his authority?
options: A) Sheila Birling
B) Arthur Birling
C) Eric Birling
D) Edna
cbt_questions.answer: B) Arthur Birling

cbt_questions.question: What is the name of the Birlings' domestic servant?
options: A) Martha
B) Edna
C) Sarah
D) Clara
cbt_questions.answer: B) Edna

cbt_questions.question: How does Edna function symbolically in the play?
options: A) As the comic relief
B) As the silent, marginalized working-class figure serving the wealthy upper class
C) As a secret detective
D) As Arthur Birling's secret partner
cbt_questions.answer: B) As the silent, marginalized working-class figure serving the wealthy upper class

cbt_questions.question: Why is the setting of 1912 significant to a 1945 audience?
options: A) It allowed the audience to laugh at outdated fashion
B) It was written right after WWII; the 1912 setting allowed Priestley to use dramatic irony to mock Arthur Birling's blind optimism before two world wars and the General Strike
C) It was the year Queen Victoria died
D) It represented a golden era of British socialism
cbt_questions.answer: B) It was written right after WWII; the 1912 setting allowed Priestley to use dramatic irony to mock Arthur Birling's blind optimism before two world wars and the General Strike

cbt_questions.question: What does the ring symbolize when Gerald gives it back to Sheila and she returns it?
options: A) Eternal love
B) The superficiality of upper-class engagements broken by moral truth, though Sheila accepts it back later when Gerald reverts to denial
C) A family heirloom lost in the war
D) A bribe
cbt_questions.answer: B) The superficiality of upper-class engagements broken by moral truth, though Sheila accepts it back later when Gerald reverts to denial

cbt_questions.question: What does Eric's heavy drinking reveal about his character and family life?
options: A) He is a professional bartender
B) Underlying tension, guilt, and the stifling, emotionally repressed nature of the Birling household
C) His love for French wine
D) That he is an athletic champion
cbt_questions.answer: B) Underlying tension, guilt, and the stifling, emotionally repressed nature of the Birling household

cbt_questions.question: What does Inspector Goole show to each family member individually that no one else sees at the same time?
options: A) A pistol
B) A photograph of Eva Smith
C) A suicide note
D) A stolen watch
cbt_questions.answer: B) A photograph of Eva Smith

cbt_questions.question: Why is the mystery of whether it was the *same* girl in everyone's story left ambiguous?
options: A) Because Priestley forgot to write the ending
B) Because the Inspector emphasizes that collective guilt and collective social responsibility matter more than individual legal identity
C) Because Eva Smith had an identical twin
D) Because the actors lost the script
cbt_questions.answer: B) Because the Inspector emphasizes that collective guilt and collective social responsibility matter more than individual legal identity

cbt_questions.question: How does Arthur Birling view the working class?
options: A) As equal partners in industry
B) As cheap labor and commodities to be exploited for profit rather than human beings
C) As future political leaders
D) With deep affectionate friendship
cbt_questions.answer: B) As cheap labor and commodities to be exploited for profit rather than human beings

cbt_questions.question: What is the core moral message J.B. Priestley promotes through the play?
options: A) Never trust police inspectors
B) Society is interconnected; we must look out for one another and share collective responsibility
C) Capitalism always brings world peace
D) Parents should never listen to their children
cbt_questions.answer: B) Society is interconnected; we must look out for one another and share collective responsibility

cbt_questions.question: How does Sheila's perspective on her father change by the end of the play?
options: A) She admires his business acumen more than ever
B) She loses respect for his lack of moral conscience and inability to learn from the experience
C) She decides to take over his company
D) She agrees to marry someone else
cbt_questions.answer: B) She loses respect for his lack of moral conscience and inability to learn from the experience

cbt_questions.question: What role does class prejudice play in Sybil Birling's treatment of Eva Smith?
options: A) She treats her with excessive maternal sympathy
B) She assumes working-class women do not have moral feelings, fine sensibilities, or genuine suffering
C) She invites her to live in their home
D) She offers her a job as a maid
cbt_questions.answer: B) She assumes working-class women do not have moral feelings, fine sensibilities, or genuine suffering

cbt_questions.question: What dramatic function does the cyclical nature of the play's final moments serve?
options: A) It confuses the audience
B) It suggests that if society refuses to learn its moral lesson, humanity is doomed to repeat its errors in endless cycles of judgment ('fire and blood')
C) It proves the Inspector was a ghost
D) It shows that time travel is real
cbt_questions.answer: B) It suggests that if society refuses to learn its moral lesson, humanity is doomed to repeat its errors in endless cycles of judgment ('fire and blood')

cbt_questions.question: Why is 'An Inspector Calls' regarded as a masterpiece of British drama?
options: A) For its elaborate musical dance numbers
B) For its brilliant fusion of an engaging thriller mystery with a profound socialist-morality critique of human conscience
C) For its realistic depiction of outer space travel
D) For its use of Shakespearean verse
cbt_questions.answer: B) For its brilliant fusion of an engaging thriller mystery with a profound socialist-morality critique of human conscience
